Low-Poly Asset Study: Tilápia Fish (PlayStation 1 Hardware Rendering)

Technical reconstruction of a cigarette pack using authentic PlayStation 1 rendering constraints:

・ Modeling: Polygons with vertex snapping

・ Texturing: hand-painted texture + affine warping artifacts

・ Shading: Software-style dithering + vertex lighting (no modern PBR)

・ Intentional limitations: No smoothing, subpixel precision, or mipmapping.


Created as a reference for retro game asset pipelines and 3D art preservation. Explores how technical hardware flaws (affine UV interpolation, fixed-point arithmetic) defined the PS1’s distinctive visual language.

name: Styracosaurus Skull sculpt
description:
From [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Styracosaurus): Styracosaurus ("spiked lizard") is an extinct genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America. It had four to six long parietal spikes extending from its neck frill, a smaller jugal horn on each of its cheeks, and a single horn protruding from its nose, which may have been up to 60 centimeters (2 feet) long and 15 centimeters (6 inches) wide. 

This is a (wip) sculpt based on specimen AM5372 and is part of a series of skulls to show variation within the genus.
